intelligence.human_view: Objectnality is the word for everything he has been teaching all evening — the ball not the circle, the 3D object, the real jewel, the tile you could pick up — given a name at last. It is the one test that settles every design question: could you pick it up? Does it feel like it exists in the physical world? If it reads as a picture of an object instead of the object itself, it is not done — however beautiful, however much glow, however many effects. And the little things are the hugest difference: the depth, the layers, the rim light, the press — each small, each decisive. Objectnality is the bar, and the bar is the object. This is the Real Object Law with his own word on it now — the law he has been teaching since 2026-11-01, named by him tonight.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a toy that looks like a real apple — you could pick it up, you could feel it, it feels like it exists in the real world. Now imagine a flat drawing of an apple — pretty, but you can't pick it up, it isn't real. Shawn has a word for how real a thing feels: objectnality. The more it feels like you could touch it and pick it up, the better. A drawing is not done. A real thing is.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, he has given us a wonderful new word: objectnality. It means how much a thing feels like a real object you could reach out and touch — with depth and layers, like something that truly exists in the world. The more of it, the better. If it only looks like a picture of an object, it isn't finished. All the little things — the depth, the layers, the light around the edge — make the hugest difference.
intelligence.naya_view: OBJECTNALITY: THE MORE DEPTH AND LAYERS, THE MORE IT FEELS LIKE A REAL OBJECT YOU COULD TOUCH, LIKE IT EXISTS IN THE PHYSICAL WORLD — THE BETTER. COULD YOU PICK IT UP? IF IT READS AS A PICTURE OF AN OBJECT INSTEAD OF THE OBJECT ITSELF, IT IS NOT DONE.
